findings.description: The reports archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block (nor an SSE argument), so stored objects are not encrypted with an explicitly configured KMS key.
The ledger exports bucket, which holds financial data, defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored objects without a configured default encryption key.
The model artifacts bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects are stored without an explicitly configured default encryption key.
The runbooks bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored objects have no explicitly configured default encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the reports bucket and no private ACL is set, leaving it without an explicit boundary preventing public exposure via bucket policy or ACL.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the ledger exports bucket, leaving no explicit safeguard against public ACLs or bucket policies exposing financial data.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the model artifacts bucket, leaving it without an explicit guard against public exposure via bucket policy or ACL.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the runbooks bucket, leaving no explicit boundary preventing public access being enabled later via policy or ACL.

findings.issue_category: log-delivery-write ACL on sensitive log bucket
findings.description: The audit trail bucket uses the legacy canned ACL 'log-delivery-write', which grants the S3 log delivery group WRITE and READ_ACP permissions on the bucket storing audit logs, broadening access to audit evidence and relying on legacy ACL semantics.
